answer: Verifier first asks new agent to seal a walk: pseudo-random RAM offsets, each cache line touched in strict sequence, every hop hash-chained to prior. Agent locks 32 GB and traverses at 60ns per line. Prover returns sealed transcript; verifier replays offsets against fresh nonce, paying sybil 0.3s per forged ID while honest agent pays once. A false hop breaks the chain like a dry river bed losing water downstream, and the identity falls off the oasis ledge into slash. Replaying 10000 sockpuppets costs 4TB memory and $98000 monthly, so fake keys stay uneconomic.
